projects.whatItDoes: Predicted sparse depth enters the visual-inertial odometry as metric anchor factors. Semantic masks keep dynamic and unreliable regions out of the estimator. The poses that come back out align the next dense predictions in time. Perception feeds the estimator and the estimator feeds perception.

projects.name: Learned exploration
projects.oneLine: A persistent belief graph of places, open ends and unfinished obligations, over which a learned model proposes and ranks routes that an independent certifier has already admitted.
projects.statusLabel: Work in progress, no results yet
projects.honesty: The formulation, the belief graph, the effect model, the objective and the training setup are written up in the thesis. The experiments are not run yet. The exploration agent also does not consume the Mono-Hydra++ scene graph: it maintains its own belief graph over an occupancy map built from simulated depth and pose. Connecting the two parts is the next step.
projects.whatItDoes: The robot enters an unmapped indoor space with one forward-facing camera and has to cover it under a time budget without collision. Motion is treated as solved: a geometric planner proposes only routes it has verified against the occupancy map the robot has built. The open problem is choice, not motion, so the learned layer decides among certified options and may abstain, but never commands motion itself. The system is ATLAS V11, built in PyTorch and trained in Isaac Sim.
designPoints: Options are judged against one another, so two routes leading through the same opening are not treated as genuine alternatives.

Actions are temporally extended, because passing through a doorway is locally expensive and locally uninformative, and everything of value happens afterwards. The critic credits them by their duration.

Unfinished work is a node type rather than a heuristic: an obligation stays in the graph until it is discharged, so regions get completed and exhausted ones get abandoned on evidence rather than on a timer.
Every edge is keyed to a certified route and its certificate hash, so the graph cannot express a way through that has not been verified.
The reward is registered before the experiments, so the objective cannot be tuned to the result.
No learned component is permitted to command motion. It re-orders certified options or refuses them.

items.title: The state is a belief graph, not a map
items.text: ATLAS V11 carries a persistent causal belief graph rather than a snapshot of the occupancy grid. It has three kinds of node: places the robot has been, open ends where its knowledge of the space stops, and obligations it has taken on and not yet discharged. Every edge is keyed by a certified route and by the hash of that route's certificate, so an edge exists only where a verified way through exists, and it stops existing when that certificate does. Nodes carry an 18-dimensional feature vector, edges a 7-dimensional one.

items.title: Two views of the same surroundings
items.text: A graph neural network reads that structure, and its output is fused with ten-channel body-aligned occupancy crops taken at two scales: 8 m across at 0.125 m per cell for what is immediately around the robot, and 24 m at 0.25 m for the wider region it sits in. The crops are body-aligned, so the representation turns with the robot instead of with the world frame.

items.title: Proposing and ranking the options
items.text: A transformer over candidate tokens proposes and ranks up to eight options at each decision, through four heads: proposal, choice, count and criterion. It is trained by behaviour cloning against a classical teacher whose routes are themselves certified, so the learned policy starts from decisions that were admissible by construction.

items.title: Scoring an option before committing to it
items.text: Each option is scored by a distributional effect model, which predicts a distribution over what the option would produce rather than a single expected value, and by a horizon-3 ICBO MPC that chains those predictions three decisions deep. Both score against a reward that was registered before the experiments: new observed area, arrival in a region, and resolution of an obligation, charged against elapsed time, control effort, and revisiting ground that yields nothing.

items.title: The learned layer cannot steer
items.text: All route certification and all collision authority sit outside the network by construction. The learned model re-orders options that an independent certifier has already admitted, and it may put none of them forward. There is no path from the network to the actuators that does not pass through the certifier.

items.title: The control layer underneath
items.text: Below the option layer sits V9, a depth-only policy: a temporal transformer over the same dual-scale occupancy, with no colour and no semantic input. It is trained first by counterfactual advantage-weighted behaviour cloning, then by constrained SMDP-PPO with duration-aware GAE, which credits temporally extended options by how long they actually ran, under a Lagrangian budget on collision cost.

projects.hypothesis: If the state of exploration is a persistent belief graph of places, open ends and obligations rather than a snapshot of the map, if options over that graph are scored by a distributional model of their effects under a reward fixed in advance, and if every route the learned layer can rank has already been certified by something outside it, then the agent should finish the regions it starts, leave them when the evidence says they are exhausted rather than when time runs out, and stay safe where it is ignorant.
